title: How can you mark points that are the same distance from P?
description: A point P is marked and many points are marked four centimetres from it with a ruler. The video turns the ruler about P again and again and watches the dots form a round shape. Keeko raises the doubt about where the ruler should start.
teaching_notes: One idea: points at one fixed distance from P lie all round P. Watch for children who start the measure from the end of the ruler, or who mark all the points in one direction.

source: Mark a point P in your notebook. Then mark as many points as possible, in different directions, that are 4 cm away from P.
video_script.why: The child marks points at one fixed distance from P in many directions and sees them gather in a round shape.
video_script.substitution: Turn the ruler about P and mark a dot at four centimetres each time.
video_script.anchor: A point P in the middle of a page
video_script.wrong_answer: put the end of the ruler on P
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko puts the end of the ruler on P. A small gap lies before the zero mark, so every dot lands closer to P than four centimetres.
video_script.payoff_line: Each dot is exactly four centimetres from P.

final_answer.value: all the points lie on a round curve around P, each 4 cm from P
final_answer.spoken: all the points lie on a round curve around P, each exactly four centimetres from P

maths_rules: Every dot is at 4 cm from P, measured with the zero mark of the ruler on P.
A different direction gives a different dot at the same distance 4 cm.
With many dots in every direction the dots join into a round curve around P.
video_script.design: One idea: many points at one distance from P lie all round P. Assumes a ruler. Wrong idea: the end of the ruler on P. P stays all video.

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>All the dots you mark lie on a round curve around P.
Each dot is exactly four centimetres from P.
With enough dots, they join into a circle.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a ruler with a small gap before its zero mark; the end of the ruler on P and the dot landing short of 4 cm; the bubble is struck out in the warning colour

marks.doubt: a bubble shows the end of the ruler on P
marks.gap: the small gap before the zero mark glows

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko wants to put the end of the ruler on P, since the ruler starts there.
<bookmark mark='gap'/>Look closely at the ruler. On many rulers, a small gap lies before the zero mark.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>That gap puts every dot closer to P than four centimetres.
The zero mark goes on P, not the end of the ruler.
